main_text.p: Voluptates praecipuè exturba, & invi- fissimas habe: Latronum more, quos phi- letas Ægyptii vocant, in hoc nos am- plectentes, ut strangulent. Atqui Hesio- dus etiam, aliíque Græci scriptores ha- bent. Ab illis igitur (quis dubitet?) Angli, to filch, (vel ut alii propiùs ad originem scribunt, to filtch) & a fil- cher.
Σῆρες [?], fauni, (de quibus inter alios μαγαίρης parens in De Satyr. Poësi:) satyri; Anglis satyres, nymphæ: larvæ, lemures.
Φόρμος, teges, storea. quæ pluribus olim, (de quo aliquid ad Theophrasti Characteres :) hodiéque vice scamni, aut cubilis. Hinc Anglis, a foutme, scamnum: fedile.
Φλάω, contundo, &c. φλάσμα, pro Φλάσμα, Hippocrati, &c. contusio; a flaw: ruptura.
Φλάζω, παφλάζω, férveo, æstuo; to flaw. nisi ex φλύζω, unde φλύσις, puftu-la. οἰνόφλυξ, quasi vino bulliens: ebrius. De vino quoque Angli.
Φείδω, habere, agere; to faire: ut εἴχεσθαι χαλῶς; to faire well: to faire ill.

page.notes: The Greek words are only partly legible on the scan; uncertain Greek is marked [?] or should be checked. Marginal marks on the right are handwritten and were not transcribed. Show-through from the facing page is ignored.
